item.title: GovBrief Today #629
item.description: Donald Trump told a North Carolina campaign rally that Marines poisoned at Camp Lejeune will have their claims settled only if Republicans keep Congress. For more than three decades, the Marine Corps piped toxic water into the homes where Marines raised their children. Hundreds of thousands of claims still sit unsettled. "If we don't win, there's no money," he said Tuesday, as the military he commands fights a war in Iran. At the same rally, he touted a $1.5 billion Pentagon loan to a North Carolina chipmaker, and that deal doesn't hinge on the vote. Only the service members, their loved ones and the civilian workers who drank the water at Lejeune have to wait for the election returns to learn their fate. item.title: Nothing says "healthy society" quite like gambling ads interrupted by a plea to feed hungry fucking schoolchildren.
item.description: Had the radio on at work today. CJAY 92 here in Calgary. Gambling ad. Another gambling ad. More gambling ads. And nestled between all that corporate enthusiasm for separating people from their money? A request for volunteers to deliver brown bag lunches to hungry schoolchildren. Jesus fucking Christ. We've somehow built a society where gambling gets a marketing budget, but feeding children requires charity, volunteers, and the goodwill of strangers. One industry spends millions convincing people to gamble their money away. Meanwhile, we're asking ordinary people to donate their time so kids don't have to sit through math class on an empty stomach. And before anyone misses the point, the volunteers are doing something wonderful. They're filling a gap that shouldn't fucking exist. The obscenity isn't the charity. It's that we need the charity in the first place. Alberta is one of the wealthiest places in Canada. A hungry child shouldn't be a fundraising opportunity. Feeding them should be a goddamn priority. #Alberta #Calgary #ChildPoverty #FoodSecurity #GamblingAds #PublicPolicy #Education #UCPcircus #DanielleSmithIsACunt
